title: Sinkers
tagline: Drop deep. Fill the row. Ride the bubbles.
teaser: Shapes sink slowly through a glowing aquarium. Slide them, spin them, then send them plunging — the farther they fall, the more they score. Fill a row and it bursts into a column of bubbles. Born as a tiny, deliberately unreadable program in 1989.

manPage.synopsis: sinkers — slide and spin shapes as they sink through a tank of water; plunge them deep for points and fill rows to burst them into bubbles.
manPage.description: Chris Torek and Darren F. Provine's falling-blocks game began as a winner of the 1989 International Obfuscated C Code Contest and reached Berkeley's games in 1992. In it, rows score nothing: points come from landing a shape and from how far you drop it, times the level. Sinkers makes that drop the heart of the game, in an aquarium of glassy pebbles.

howToPlay: Slide with ← and →, turn with ↑ or Z and X; ↓ sinks faster, Space plunges straight down.
The farther a shape plunges, the more it scores; fill a row from wall to wall and it bursts.
Plunges in a row build a depth combo that multiplies your next burst; letting one settle on its own starts it over.
